See3 Nephi 18:1–9. Joseph Smith also broke bread “after the ancient order” in the School of the Prophets. Zebedee Coltrin remembered how the Prophet blessed the emblems and then broke the warm, freshly baked bread into pieces the size of his fist and invited the men, each with a glass of wine, to eat until they were filled. See Salt Lake School of the Prophets, Minutes, Oct. 3, 1883, 58–59, Church History Library, Salt Lake City. George Q. Cannon observed in 1897, with some regret, that larger meeting sizes had led to greater formality in the administration of the sacrament, as evidenced by the smaller pieces of bread and the manner of their distribution among the congregation. See Cannon, “Editorial Thoughts,”Juvenile Instructor,Jan. 15, 1897, 52–53; quoted in Bray, “The Lord’s Supper in Early Mormonism,” 64.
